prompt: Two generating functions each have coefficient one at every non-negative degree. What does the coefficient at degree four of their product count?

options.text: Only choosing four items from the first factor.
options.explanation: The second factor may contribute part or all of the total.

options.text: All ordered sequences of four labelled items.
options.explanation: These factors record counts by size, not labelled sequence positions.

options.text: The possible splits of a total of four between the two factors.
options.explanation: Multiplication adds degrees; the coefficient sums the counts for compatible pairs of degrees.

options.text: Only splits where both parts are positive.
options.explanation: Each factor has a constant term, so either part can be zero.

workedExample: To form a term of degree four, pair a term from the first factor with one whose degree completes the total in the second. The splits are zero/four, one/three, two/two, three/one and four/zero. Each contributes once. This is convolution of the coefficient sequences.
